note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
“He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” That does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house; you may be storing up treasures in heaven.

“Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.” As in the wilderness, when thousands of men gave their half shekels for the sanctuary, and as in Babylon, when our fathers made a collection according to every man's power, you give according to your power and as you purpose in your heart. Giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money. Many do not have the spirit to give; if you have trouble coming up out of your pocket for the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith.

precepts.text: He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.
precepts.point: The rich cast in much, but the poor widow threw in two mites, and he says she cast in more than they all, for they cast in of their abundance, but she of her want did cast in all that she had.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
The rich cast much into the treasury, and a poor widow threw in two mites. “Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.”

Paul lays down the rule: “He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” The rich gave much and sowed sparingly, because it was out of their abundance; the widow gave two mites and sowed bountifully, because it was all she had. The measure is not the sum but what it cost the giver, and the reaping follows that.

“Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people.” That is what they were doing when they ministered to the saints and taught salvation in the Messiah.

For them to stay a whole year, the church had to support that movement. How can we stay somewhere a whole year if the bounty is not made up? We go for a week and then have to come back. That is what the bounty is for.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

precepts.why:
“For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.” Achaia was ready a year ago and their zeal provoked very many, and Paul sent the brethren before to “make up beforehand your bounty”: your bounty is your money, “that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.”

The money he was collecting had nothing to do with covetousness. That is why verse 1 says “as touching the ministering to the saints”: these were men and women of the body who had need.

points: “For as touching the ministering to the saints”: that is what you see us doing, developing, growing, instructing how we minister to the saints, and the saints of the Most High are you, the nation of Israel. “It is superfluous for me to write to you”: superfluous meaning extra.

“For I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal hath provoked very many.” Don’t put us in the category of the Christian church and the other religious organizations: our mission is to minister to the saints. Paul was boasting about where they were going, and telling this church to step its game up, lest they of Macedonia come and find them unprepared.

“Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty”: the bounty is the money, so we can minister to the saints. It should not come out of our own pockets. “That the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.” When we tell you to donate, it is so we can go and minister to the saints, not for covetousness like the Christian church, where you give your money and watch them get multimillion-dollar homes, cars and jets.
